prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a clear TWO-PANEL comparison of gameplay screens for an original flat top-down Game Boy Color-inspired action adventure, working title DAWN ISLE. This is a proposed gameplay visual, not a real implementation. Wide landscape board, two equal nearly square screens side by side, cream margin, tiny bitmap captions outside screens: left "VILLAGE PATH", right "FIRST DUNGEON".
Both screens must feel like authentic modest late-1990s portable pixel art, with a 160x144-style low logical resolution and simple 16-pixel tile logic, hard nearest-neighbor-style edges, deliberately chunky sprites, flat overhead camera, no perspective vanishing point, no isometric diamond grid. Keep textures sparse and repeating. No modern HD pixel-art complexity, no painterly shading, no soft gradients, no bloom, no 3D, no realistic detail. Limited palettes, flat fills, maximum around 4 colors within an individual sprite or tile where practical.
Original young hero appears consistently in BOTH screens: tiny dark-haired sprite, amber jacket, red scarf, brown boots, simple short silver blade, no pointed cap. Original world, original creatures, no existing franchise names, logos, character designs, maps or symbols.
LEFT SCREEN: an actual small traversable overworld tile-map screen. Pale tan winding path goes from lower center past a tiny warm orange-roofed cottage on the left, a stone shrine on upper left, a few compact dark green trees and a blue 2-tile stream to right, up toward a ruined watchtower entrance at upper right. Small keeper NPC by the shrine. One original round coral beetle enemy on path away from NPC. Hero near center facing up. A single small one-tile dark pit beside the stream visibly blocks a side shortcut; most main route is open and continuous. World feels like a friendly surviving village next to fallen ruins: bright green village tiles transitioning to purple-gray masonry near tower. No sky or horizon.
RIGHT SCREEN: actual dungeon room on a square tile grid. Dark navy stone walls border gray-purple floor. Closed original wooden chest has been opened at left; an item pedestal displays a tiny cyan winged-boot icon. A one-tile-wide horizontal pit crosses part of the room, with obvious walkable landing beyond it and a north door leading toward an orange glow from the watchfire. Hero is mid-dash across one tile of pit, three small cyan motion pixels behind feet. One stone beetle enemy faces wall at upper right, its pale yellow core visible. At least one short readable directional puzzle conveyed by layout; no text tutorial block.
BOTH SCREENS have an identical cream HUD strip at top: three simple red hearts left, sword icon and selected-item icon right. On left selected icon shield, on right selected icon boots. No minimap, no currency, no XP, no large wordmark, no dialogue panel or marketing sentences. Clear compact tile-based game screens with same sprite scale. These are flat and charming, resembling the graphical constraints of a GBC game rather than modern pixel illustration. No hardware mockup. Landscape overall canvas.
